newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks powered by New York rallies.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks powered by New York rallies.

text.p: Argentine stocks showed strong gains in brisk trading Tuesday spurred by the dramatic rise on New York markets, dealers said.

"Investors are perhaps overly bullish after the release of today's U.S. economic indicators, but the U.S. long bond yield slipped under the psychological barrier of seven percent and that's a very positive sign," said Dario Lizzano, head of research at Santander Investment.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 1.7 percent to 728.66, while floor volume swelled to 29.2 million pesos from a paltry 9.7 million pesos Monday.
Floor volume also surged to 104.4 million pesos from 41.2 million Thursday.
"New York really gave us a boost today -- players who were on the sidelines rushed back in to cash in on the rally," another trader said.
The U.S. long bond yield dived to 6.98 percent from 7.12 percent after the release of a much tamer than expected U.S. Employment Cost Index, while the Dow surged 2.6 percent.
"The tone should stay firm although the arrival of company results from now on will probably make the bolsa more selective," Lizzano said.
Winners smashed losers 47 to 11 while 14 issues closed flat.

The top market performer was steelmaker Acindar, which shot up 4.7 percent, continuing Monday's rebound from losses blamed last week on lower-than-expected quarterly profits. Other top gainers were Telecom and Telefonica, which rose 3.5 percent and 2.8 percent, respectively, and holding company Perez Companc, up 2.4 percent.
The only losers were carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, off 1.4 percent and 0.9 percent, respectively, on volatility induced by Brazil trade jitters.
